summary.text: Dark matter is an invisible, hypothetical form of matter that does not interact with electromagnetic radiation, including light.
It is implied by gravitational effects that general relativity cannot explain unless more matter is present than can be observed.
Dark matter is thought to act as gravitational scaffolding for cosmic structures, and in the standard model it makes up 85% of the universe's total mass.

facts.label: Share of mass
facts.value: About 85% of the universe's total mass

facts.label: How it interacts
facts.value: Not known to act except through gravity

facts.label: Leading candidates
facts.value: WIMPs, axions, or primordial black holes

items.prompt: Why is it so hard to catch dark matter in a laboratory?

options.label: It is not known to act on ordinary matter except by gravity
It is far too hot to be held in any container
It disappears the very moment it is touched
It only exists far outside of all the galaxies

items.explain: Dark matter is not known to interact with ordinary baryonic matter and radiation except through gravity.

items.prompt: Galaxies at the edge of the Coma Cluster moved far too fast for the visible galaxies' gravity to hold them. What did Zwicky infer?

options.label: The galaxies were slowly flying apart
The measurements of the speeds were wrong
Hidden mass was supplying the extra pull that kept the cluster together
The galaxies were much heavier than they looked

items.explain: The visible galaxies' gravity was far too small for such fast orbits, so Zwicky inferred unseen matter provided the mass to hold the cluster together.

items.prompt: Some astrophysicists propose changing the laws of gravity instead of adding dark matter. What problem do those proposals face?

options.label: They contradict every observation made so far
They need dark matter to be hot
They only work for the Solar System
None can describe every piece of observational evidence at the same time

items.explain: None of the proposed modified gravity theories can describe all the observational evidence at once, suggesting some form of dark matter would still be required.

items.prompt: In the 1970s, astronomers measured how fast stars and gas orbit in the outer parts of spiral galaxies. What did that support?

options.label: Galaxies are slowing down with age
Galaxies are surrounded by halos of unseen matter
Galaxies are mostly empty space
Galaxies all contain the same number of stars

items.explain: Rotation curves were one observation serving as evidence for galactic halos of dark matter.

items.prompt: After the Big Bang, what did dark matter do on large scales?

options.label: Spread out evenly in every direction in space
Gathered together into a single enormous ball
Clumped along narrow filaments, forming a cosmic web
Stayed locked only inside of individual galaxies

items.explain: Dark matter clumped into blobs along narrow filaments, with superclusters forming a cosmic web.

items.prompt: How did Zwicky's idea of dark matter differ from the modern one?

options.label: He thought it was a new kind of particle
He thought it was made of black holes
He thought it was a form of energy
He thought it was ordinary matter that gives off no light

items.explain: Zwicky considered dark matter to be non-luminous ordinary matter, unlike modern theories.
